findings.text: Command block holds four sixty four bit slots with a native order view and a little endian view; allocation clears all four native slots before encoding, and every builder converts native slots to little endian form before posting.

Core routing fields: command opcode occupies low byte of first word; device identity occupies upper half of first word; event identity occupies low half of second word; physical interrupt identity occupies upper half of second word; table size occupies low five bits of second word; sequence number occupies middle high bits of first word; translation node list occupies low sixteen bits of second word.

Address and target fields are stored shifted: translation table base shifted right by eight lives in middle of third word; redistributor target shifted right by sixteen lives in middle of third word; collection identifier lives low in third word; validity is top bit of third word; virtual table base shifted right by sixteen lives in middle of fourth word with its size low in fourth word; virtual configuration base shifted right by sixteen lives in middle of first word.

Virtualization fields: virtual processor identity lives middle high in second word; virtual interrupt identity lives low half of third word; doorbell physical identity lives upper half of third word; doorbell valid is bit zero of third word while separate doorbell present flag is top bit of third word; allocation and pass through flags are bits eight and nine of first word; default doorbell for map lives low in second word and for move lives low in fourth word.

Virtual software generated interrupt fields all live in first word: interrupt number in bits above thirty two, priority high nibble in low twenties, group in bit ten, clear in bit nine, enable in bit eight.
Every command builder starts from a zeroed block and ends by translating all four native words to little endian form, giving big endian hosts a consistent wire order.

Device mapping derives table size as binary logarithm of requested entry count minus one, translates the device table virtual base to physical, and encodes opcode plus device identity plus size plus address plus validity; unmap uses same path with validity cleared.

Collection mapping encodes collection identity plus target plus validity; event mapping encodes device plus event plus physical interrupt plus resolved collection; move encodes device plus event plus destination collection; discard, invalidate, trigger and clear encode only device plus event; invalidate all encodes only collection; all except device and collection mapping resolve the affected collection from device and event state and validate it before returning it as synchronization target.

Virtual invalidate all encodes only virtual processor identity; virtual map encodes device plus processor plus event plus doorbell plus virtual identity with doorbell forced to reserved value 1023 on newer hardware or when doorbell disabled; virtual move encodes same plus doorbell valid set; virtual processor move encodes sequence plus node list plus processor plus target and on newer hardware sets doorbell present plus default doorbell; doorbell invalidate and virtual SGI are rejected on older hardware.

Virtual processor mapping tracks an attach count: map increments and unmap decrements, with allocation flag set only on first map or last unmap; unmap on older hardware still needs explicit synchronization while newer hardware treats it as self synchronizing; map programs target redistributor offset plus table base and size, and on newer hardware also programs allocation plus configuration base plus default doorbell with pass through never advertised.

Virtual invalidate, trigger and clear reuse the physical descriptor layout for device and event but resolve a virtual processor through an event to virtual mapping instead of a collection, then encode the same physical opcode.

Single command emission serializes on the node lock with interrupts saved across allocation of the main entry, building and cache handling, optional allocation and building of a follow up synchronization entry, sampling of the read index and publishing of the write index; the lock is released before waiting for completion.

Command queue is a fixed ring with base pointer and advancing write pointer that wraps to base; fullness is judged by comparing next write slot against the hardware read register; publishing writes the byte offset of the next slot to the write register; completion polls the read register with wrap aware linearization until the observed index reaches the published index.

Before publishing, each entry is either flushed from cache to point of coherency when the node requires it or ordered by a barrier otherwise; physical commands are followed by a sync targeting the affected collection address and virtual commands by a virtual sync targeting the processor identity.

Thin send helpers fill a descriptor union member for one operation and delegate to the single physical or single virtual emitter; virtual map and move helpers first look up the stored virtual mapping to obtain processor, virtual identity and doorbell state, and processor map selects the collection indexed by the processor.

Allocation spins up to about one second polling for drain and on expiry logs a rate limited queue fault and aborts the request; completion wait spins similarly and on expiry logs observed versus target offsets and the emitter logs the failed builder; failure to allocate the follow up synchronization entry still publishes the main entry.
